name: arclang
description: Arcadia MBSE as code: diagnostics with rules, outline, completion from the metamodel, hover, go to definition, rename, formatting, the viewpoint diagrams beside the source, the production gate, Arcadia transitions, the @arclang chat participant and compiler tools for agent mode, the ArcLang MCP server. Everything comes from the ArcLang compiler.

virtualWorkspaces.description: In a virtual workspace (the web playground) the compiler runs in WebAssembly on the open files.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In an untrusted workspace the compiler is not run on its files: no diagnostics, commands, diagrams or tools until the workspace is trusted. The executable and the MCP server command can only be set in user settings.

arclang.binary.markdownDescription: The `arclang` executable: a name on the PATH or an absolute path. The extension runs `arclang lsp --stdio`, `arclang diagram`, `arclang check`, `arclang gate`, `arclang transition`, `arclang export`, `arclang import`, `arclang set`, `arclang rename`. User setting only: a workspace cannot choose the executable the extension runs.

arclang.diagrams.refreshOnSave.description: Redraw the open diagrams every time their model is saved.

arclang.gate.standard.description: The standard the production gate judges against.

arclang.ai.repairAttempts.markdownDescription: When what an AI wrote does not compile (a model of `@arclang`, the edits of **Ask AI**), how many times the compiler's errors are sent back to it before the answer is shown as refused.

enumDescriptions: The language models VS Code offers (GitHub Copilot or any other extension's); pick one with arclang.ai.vscodeModel.
Anthropic Claude (key: ArcLang: Set AI API key).
OpenAI (key: ArcLang: Set AI API key).
Azure OpenAI: arclang.ai.endpoint, arclang.ai.azureDeployment and arclang.ai.apiVersion, and a key.
Mistral AI (key: ArcLang: Set AI API key).
Google Gemini (key: ArcLang: Set AI API key).
Ollama on this machine: no key, nothing leaves it.
Any server with the OpenAI chat completions API (LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp, LiteLLM…) at arclang.ai.endpoint; key optional.
No AI: nothing is ever sent.
arclang.ai.provider.markdownDescription: The AI behind **Ask AI** (⌘I on a selection), the impact suggestions and `@arclang`. API keys are never settings: run **ArcLang: Set AI API key** (stored in the OS keychain through VS Code's secret storage). User setting only: a workspace cannot redirect the requests.

arclang.ai.model.markdownDescription: The model, as the provider spells it. Empty: the provider's default (`claude-opus-5-5` for Anthropic, `gpt-5` for OpenAI, `mistral-large-latest`, `gemini-2.5-pro`, `llama3.1` for Ollama; the deployment for Azure). **ArcLang: Choose the AI model** lists them.

arclang.ai.vscodeModel.markdownDescription: With the `vscode-lm` provider: the VS Code language model to use, by id or family (for example `gpt-4.1`, `claude-sonnet-4`). Empty: the first Copilot model. **ArcLang: Choose the AI model** picks it from the list.

arclang.ai.endpoint.markdownDescription: The base URL of the provider. Empty: its public API (`https://api.anthropic.com`, `https://api.openai.com/v1`, `https://api.mistral.ai/v1`, `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta`, `http://localhost:11434` for Ollama). Required for `azure-openai` (`https://<resource>.openai.azure.com`) and `openai-compatible` (for example `http://localhost:1234/v1`). User setting only.

arclang.ai.azureDeployment.description: Azure OpenAI: the name of the deployment to call.

arclang.ai.apiVersion.description: Azure OpenAI: the api-version of the requests.

arclang.ai.temperature.markdownDescription: Sampling temperature. `null`: the provider's default (some models accept no other).

arclang.ai.timeoutSeconds.description: The longest wait for the provider's first byte, and between two parts of its answer.

enumDescriptions: After an edit, the compiler's consequences (broken traces, new findings, gate blockers) show in the Suggestions pane; the AI is asked when you click "Propose changes with AI" or "Analyse impact".
After an edit with consequences, the AI proposes one to three changes in the Suggestions pane, each checked by the compiler. Nothing is applied without your click.
arclang.ai.suggestOnEdit.description: Impact-driven AI suggestions while editing in the workbench.

enumDescriptions: The source of the selected elements, their relationships and findings.
Also the source of their neighbours (the other ends of their relationships, their owners).
Also the whole model text (clipped to a size the model takes).
arclang.ai.contextScope.description: What the AI is shown around a selection, besides the metamodel of its kinds and the gate state.

arclang.ai.confirmBeforeSending.markdownDescription: Ask before the first request to a cloud provider (per provider and endpoint), saying what is sent and where. Local servers (`localhost`, Ollama) are not asked. User setting only.

arclang.mcp.command.markdownDescription: Command that starts the ArcLang MCP server for agent mode (for example `arclang-mcp`, or `uv run --directory /path/to/arclang/mcp-server arclang-mcp`). Empty: the server is offered only when `arclang-mcp` is on the PATH.

arclang.mcp.args.description: Arguments of the MCP server command.

arclang.diagram.theme.markdownDescription: The colour theme of every diagram, on every layer: a preset (`arclang-default`, `capella-classic`, `colorblind-safe`, `print-grayscale`, `high-contrast`, `monochrome-document`), the `id` of a team theme (`.arclang/themes/*.json` in the workspace, versioned with the model) or of one of yours (**ArcLang: Edit or create a diagram colour theme…**), or the path of an `arclang-theme.json` file. A theme that breaks a colour rule is refused and the default is drawn, with the reasons. In a dark VS Code theme, a colour theme with a dark variant draws it; any other is turned dark by inverting it.

enumDescriptions: The image keeps the sheet of its theme (white for every light theme): what a slide expects.
No sheet: the boxes and lines only, for a coloured slide.
arclang.diagram.copyBackground.description: The background of the diagram copied as an image (Copy as image, ⇧⌘C / Ctrl+Shift+C on the canvas).

chatParticipants.name: arclang
chatParticipants.description: Model in Arcadia with the compiler at hand: write, fix, explain and review ArcLang models.

commands.name: model
commands.description: Write or extend an ArcLang model from a description. The result is compiled before it is shown.

commands.name: fix
commands.description: Fix the compiler errors and findings of the open model, minimally.

commands.name: explain
commands.description: Explain the open model, an element or a finding, from what the compiler knows.

commands.name: review
commands.description: Review the open model: coverage, traces, safety, timing, against the production gate.

commands.name: transition
commands.description: Plan and apply the next Arcadia transition (OA to SA, SA to LA, LA to PA).

commands.name: agent
commands.description: Change the open model step by step through the compiler: read the elements, apply precise edits you confirm, check the result.

disambiguation.description: The user wants to write, fix, review or understand an Arcadia / ArcLang / Capella model (.arc file): requirements, functions, components, traces, safety, timing.
examples: Write the logical architecture of an emergency braking system
Why does the gate fail on this model?
Add a hazard for late braking

languageModelTools.name: arclang_check
languageModelTools.userDescription: Compile a .arc model and report the compiler's errors and rule findings.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Compiles an ArcLang (.arc) model with the ArcLang compiler and returns its errors and its findings as JSON: each finding has a rule (see arclang_rules), a severity, the element concerned and, when the compiler knows one, a fix. Use it after every edit of a model and before claiming a model is correct. Input: either the absolute path of a .arc file, or the full source text.

path.description: Absolute path of the .arc file to check.

source.description: Full ArcLang source to check instead of a file.

languageModelTools.name: arclang_gate
languageModelTools.userDescription: Run the production-readiness gate on a .arc model.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Runs the ArcLang production gate on a .arc model: a PASS/FAIL verdict against what an industrial design review requires (requirements coverage, HARA/ASIL consistency, timing budgets, ICD completeness), for a standard (iso26262, do178c, iec61508). Returns the compiler's report verbatim.

standard.description: The standard to judge against (default iso26262).

languageModelTools.name: arclang_metamodel
languageModelTools.userDescription: The ArcLang language reference, printed by the compiler.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the ArcLang language metamodel as the compiler prints it: element kinds per Arcadia level, their typed attributes, enumerations, units of quantities and the trace rules. Read it before writing ArcLang; it is the only syntax reference to trust. Optionally filtered to one element kind.

kind.description: An element kind to focus on (for example 'component', 'requirement', 'functional_chain'). Omit for the whole metamodel.

languageModelTools.name: arclang_rules
languageModelTools.userDescription: The catalogue of validation rules the compiler checks.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the catalogue of ArcLang validation rules (what arclang_check reports) as JSON: rule id, severity, what it checks and how to satisfy it.

languageModelTools.name: arclang_impact
languageModelTools.userDescription: Everything transitively affected when an element changes.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Change-impact analysis of one element of a .arc model (requirement, component, function, by id or unambiguous name): everything transitively affected through traces, allocations, exchanges and deployments, as the compiler reports it.

element.description: Element id or unambiguous name, for example REQ-AEB-004.

languageModelTools.name: arclang_transition_plan
languageModelTools.userDescription: What each Arcadia transition step would create.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: For a .arc model, says what each Arcadia transition step (oa-to-sa, sa-to-la, la-to-pa) would declare on the next level: the elements already realized and those still to create, as the compiler's JSON plan. Nothing is written.

step.description: One step; omit for every step.

languageModelTools.name: arclang_set_attribute
languageModelTools.userDescription: Set one attribute of one element, through the compiler's lossless editor.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Sets one attribute of one element of an open .arc model through the compiler's source editor: comments and layout are kept, and the edit is refused unless the edited model compiles. The change is applied in the editor as an undoable edit. Value is ArcLang source: '"text"', '25 ms', '[A, B]', 'true'.

element.description: Identifier of the element, or its name when it has no id.

languageModelTools.name: arclang_rename
languageModelTools.userDescription: Rename one element without changing its identity.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Renames one element of an open .arc model through the compiler's source editor; refused when the element is known by its name elsewhere, because its identity must not change. Applied as an undoable edit.

languageModelTools.name: arclang_model
languageModelTools.userDescription: The elements of a model as the compiler sees them, with their ids, kinds, owners and attributes.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reads an open .arc model through the compiler (arclang workbench): counts by kind, the elements (id, kind, name, owner, attributes) filtered by kind, layer or one element (then with its relationships and traces), the findings and the gate. Use it before editing to know the exact ids; the ids it lists are accepted by arclang_edit even when the text writes none.

kind.description: Only the elements of this kind (LogicalComponent, SystemFunction, Requirement...).

layer.description: Only the elements of this layer: Operational, System, Logical, Physical, Epbs, Data, Transverse.

element.description: Only this element (id or name), with what it is connected to.

languageModelTools.name: arclang_edit
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add, remove, move, rename, trace or set elements of a model; refused unless the model still compiles.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Applies a list of edits to an open .arc model through the compiler's source editor (arclang edit), in order, as one undoable change in the editor: add an element inside another, in a layer or at the top level (ports with keyword 'port in'/'port out'), add a raw declaration (exchanges, messages, transitions), remove, move, rename (identity kept), set/unset an attribute, add/remove a trace, wrap messages in a fragment. Comments and layout are kept. The whole list is refused, and nothing changes, if any edit would leave a model that does not compile; the answer says which request and why. Prefer this over rewriting the file.

items.description: One edit of the model text. op is one of set, unset, rename, add, add_raw, remove, move, add_trace, remove_trace, wrap_fragment. Elements are designated by the id the model tool lists (or the name when it writes none).

value.description: set: the value as ArcLang source: '"text"', '25 ms', '[A, B]', 'ASIL-D'.

name.description: rename: the new name; add: the name of the new element.

keyword.description: add: the declaration keyword: actor, entity, activity, function, component, node, behavior_component, 'port in', 'port out', interface, class, mission, capability, functional_chain, requirement...

attributes.description: add: [key, value] pairs written with the new element, values as ArcLang source.

declaration.description: add_raw: one declaration as ArcLang source, e.g. 'component_exchange "Flow" { from_port: "LC-A.p" to_port: "LC-B.q" }' or 'message "A" -> "B" "text"'.

container.description: add/add_raw/move: the element the declaration goes into.

layer.description: add/add_raw/move: else the layer block: operational_analysis, system_analysis, logical_architecture, physical_architecture, epbs.

layer_name.description: add/add_raw/move: the layer's name when several layers of that kind exist.

top_level.description: add/add_raw: else at the end of the file (classes, data types, traces).

kind.description: add_trace/remove_trace: satisfies, implements, realizes, allocates, verifies...; wrap_fragment: loop, opt, alt, par, seq, critical.

requests.description: The edits, applied in order on one text.

[Import a Capella model](command:arclang.import.capella)
[Import SysML v2](command:arclang.import.sysml)
[Import requirements (ReqIF)](command:arclang.import.reqif)
[New model](command:arclang.newModel)
Also: [from a SysML v2 API server](command:arclang.import.api), [from DOORS](command:arclang.import.doors).

Open a .arc or .sysml file to see its model, or bring one in.
[Import a model…](command:arclang.import)
[New model](command:arclang.newModel)
